Scope: production control, nonconforming product, monitoring and measuring resources, release of product. Criteria: ISO 9001:2015 plus customer-specific requirements. Summary: The area has a mature 5S program and good visual management. Four findings and two opportunities for improvement are recorded. Grading per QP-9.2: MAJOR = absence or total breakdown of a required process, or a situation likely to result in shipment of nonconforming product; MINOR = a single lapse or partial failure that does not by itself put product conformity at risk; OFI = no requirement breached.

Finding 1: Operator sign-off on setup verification sheets was missing for 4 of 30 sampled setups on the HMC cell. This repeats finding IA-25-21 from last year; the corrective action (sheet redesign) was implemented but has not been effective.

Finding 2: In the MRB cage, 3 of 40 bins of nonconforming parts had no red NCR tag. All 3 bins were inside the locked cage and listed on the MRB log, so they were segregated and identified in the system.

Finding 3: A 20 to 100 Nm click torque wrench (asset TW-118) used on assembly station A-4 for final bolt torque had no calibration label and was not in the calibration recall database. Operators said it was brought over from Building 1 two months ago.

"Record REC-4410
Title: Proton pump inhibitor use and risk of community-acquired pneumonia in older adults: a population-based study

Abstract: Background: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are widely prescribed to older adults. Some studies suggest an association with pneumonia. Methods: Using a regional primary care database, we identified all adults aged 65 years and over with a first hospital admission for community-acquired pneumonia between two index years (cases). For each case, up to four controls without pneumonia were matched on age, sex, general practice and calendar time. Current PPI use was defined as a prescription within 30 days before the index date. Conditional logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios adjusted for comorbidities and co-medications. Results: We included 6,112 cases and 23,904 matched controls. Current PPI use was associated with increased odds of pneumonia (adjusted OR 1.31, 95% CI 1.19 to 1.44). The association was strongest in the first 30 days after starting treatment. Conclusions: Current PPI use is associated with a modest increase in pneumonia risk in older adults; residual confounding cannot be excluded."
